title: Trump Administration to Revoke Up to 200,000 Visas in Largest Mass Revocation Ever
detail: The State Department announced Tuesday, August 25, 2026 it would revoke as many as 200,000 B1/B2 (business and tourism) visas issued between 2016 and 2026, in what officials called the largest mass visa revocation in US history. The State Department is coordinating with the Department of Homeland Security to identify and revoke the nonimmigrant visas of foreigners who entered the country claiming to be short-term visitors but subsequently filed for asylum to remain permanently. The move escalates Trump's second-term drive to reduce the number of foreign nationals living in the US and is expected to face legal challenges.

media.caption: State Department to revoke up to 200,000 B1/B2 visas from asylum seekers who entered as short-term visitors

title: Canada Announces Retaliatory Tariffs on $20 Billion of US Goods
detail: Canada announced retaliatory duties on C$27.6 billion (roughly $19.94 billion USD) of American goods on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, matching Washington's tariffs dollar-for-dollar. The counter-tariffs, taking effect September 8, impose 50% duties on steel, aluminum, furniture, and clothing; 25% on cheese, appliances, and some seafood; and 15% on electronics and tools, spanning roughly 700 US products. Prime Minister Mark Carney's government also unveiled a C$7.5 billion support package for affected businesses and workers, including cash-flow funding for small and medium-sized enterprises. The move follows the collapse of US-Canada trade talks on August 21 and the 50% US tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods that took effect that weekend.

media.caption: Canada unveils dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion of US goods, effective Sept. 8
